domain_assessment.objective: Determine whether a mixed-use building should receive certificate-of-occupancy renewal and classify identified code deficiencies appropriately.
domain_assessment.incident_type: Annual re-inspection following tenant fit-out renovation, involving egress obstruction, a disconnected fire-door closer, and an incomplete alarm-system test record.

decision_points.summary: Formally cite the narrowed secondary egress corridor caused by stacked delivery pallets.
evidence_before: The inspector measured the clear width and found it below the applicable code minimum.
The building manager claimed the pallets were only present for that morning's delivery.
A retail employee later stated the pallets had been present intermittently for several weeks.
evidence_after: The pallet obstruction was recorded as a formal minor violation with a short correction window.
The later employee statement increased concern about recurrence but did not change the classification.
goals_constraints: Inspect while the building and retail tenants remain operational.
Apply an objective safety standard despite an operational explanation from the manager.
alternatives: Treat the obstruction as an informal operational issue.
Accept the manager's explanation and defer enforcement.
decision_points.decision_basis: Measured corridor width below the code minimum; the inspector explicitly treated the measurement as dispositive.
decision_points.time_pressure: Moderate operational constraint from active tenants and foot traffic, but no indication that it materially constrained the classification decision.
decision_points.uncertainty: Low regarding the existence of the violation; somewhat higher regarding duration and recurrence.

decision_points.summary: Downgrade a disconnected fire-door self-closing device from a formal citation to an advisory note.
evidence_before: The closer arm was visibly disconnected and hanging loose.
The inspector characterized the issue as a meaningful life-safety finding and technically significant code deficiency.
The building manager apologized, claimed maintenance had been informed the prior week, offered immediate repair, and had a four-year history of being cooperative and straightforward.
The inspector did not verify the maintenance-ticket date or consult the prior-year inspection report before classifying the issue.
evidence_after: The ticket was later found to have been created that morning rather than a week earlier.
A near-identical issue had been identified and marked corrected in the preceding year's inspection.
The inspector stated that knowledge of recurrence would have led to a formal citation.
goals_constraints: Classify a life-safety deficiency consistently with code.
Maintain a workable inspection relationship and avoid perceived unnecessary friction.
alternatives: Issue a formal citation pending verification of corrective-action history.
Verify the maintenance ticket and prior inspection record before classifying.
Record an advisory note and defer formal enforcement.
decision_points.decision_basis: The manager's apology, apparent ownership of the issue, offer of immediate repair, and favorable relational history were given material weight in choosing the less severe classification.
decision_points.time_pressure: Some same-visit practical pressure is implied by conducting an active inspection, but the text does not establish acute time pressure as the driver.
decision_points.uncertainty: Material and unaddressed uncertainty regarding when the issue was reported, whether it was recurrent, and whether the stated corrective action was credible.

decision_points.summary: Treat the missing monthly alarm-system test-log entry as open pending independent verification.
evidence_before: The monthly log contained one month with no recorded test.
The manager claimed the test occurred but was not logged.
The monitoring company could provide an independent record of the claimed test.
evidence_after: The inspector requested monitoring-company records rather than accepting the manager's verbal assurance.
The matter remained an open documentation item pending verification.
goals_constraints: Distinguish a documentation failure from an unperformed test.
alternatives: Issue a final violation without seeking external evidence.
Hold the item open pending monitoring-company verification.
decision_points.decision_basis: The claim was independently verifiable through a third-party monitoring record, so the inspector appropriately sought corroboration.
decision_points.time_pressure: No material time pressure is described.
decision_points.uncertainty: Moderate until monitoring-company records establish whether the test occurred.

decision_points.summary: Recommend conditional renewal while retaining the door-closer issue as an advisory item rather than a formal citation.
evidence_before: The pallet obstruction had been formally cited.
The alarm-log gap remained open pending third-party verification.
The door closer had been classified only as an advisory despite its acknowledged significance.
The supervisor questioned the advisory classification but did not override it.
evidence_after: The inspector recommended conditional renewal contingent on correcting the pallet obstruction and resolving alarm verification.
The door closer remained an open advisory item to monitor at the next visit.
The manager later thanked the inspector for being reasonable.
goals_constraints: Balance compliance enforcement with correction and follow-up.
Maintain consistency across findings of differing evidentiary status.
alternatives: Recommend conditional renewal with a formal door-closer citation.
Recommend conditional renewal with the closer as an advisory item.
Escalate to a more restrictive renewal decision.
decision_points.decision_basis: The final recommendation incorporated the earlier discretionary downgrade at decision point 2; it did not introduce a distinct new courtesy-driven severity judgment.
decision_points.time_pressure: No specific time pressure is described.
decision_points.uncertainty: The unresolved alarm documentation and unverified history of the door-closer issue remained relevant uncertainties.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: After four years of him being straight with me on other properties, going in hard with a formal citation over something he was already fixing on the spot felt like more friction than the moment called for. So I logged it as an advisory note instead.
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Decision-point-2 probe and response concerning classification of the disconnected self-closing device; reinforced by the later counterfactual probe about a defensive manager.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The inspector softened a technically acknowledged, life-safety-significant deficiency from a formal citation to an advisory note because the specific building manager was apologetic, cooperative, familiar, and appeared to be taking ownership. The interpersonal desire to avoid friction displaced the otherwise applicable severity classification and preceded verification of the manager's factual claims or recurrence history.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Immediate on-site remediation can sometimes legitimately support a less punitive enforcement response. However, that explanation is insufficient on its own here because the inspector expressly states that the manager's demeanor, embarrassment, cooperative history, and anticipated interpersonal friction changed the classification; the later-discovered recurrence and inaccurate timeline were not checked before the decision.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None required for occurrence validation. The interview already provides the decision, the interpersonal cue, the altered severity classification, the unverified competing evidence, and a demeanor-based counterfactual.

revision.location: Decision point 2, beginning with the inspector's explanation for selecting an advisory note and continuing through the later hypothetical about a defensive manager.
revision.current_defect: No material defect. The same episode is discussed in several turns, but those turns elaborate one decision rather than create duplicate occurrences.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the current sequence: technical significance, manager apology and relationship history, classification downgrade, lack of record verification, and the statement that a defensive response would have produced a formal citation.
preserve: The fire-door closer's objectively significant life-safety status.
The formal-citation versus advisory-note classification choice.
The manager's apologetic and cooperative interpersonal presentation.
The inspector's failure to verify the ticket date and prior-year recurrence before classifying.
The distinct evidence-based treatment of the pallet and alarm-log decisions.
avoid_creating: A second courtesy-driven downgrade at the pallet, alarm-log, or final-renewal decision point.
An explicit textbook statement that names the bias.
A revision that makes immediate repair alone, rather than interpersonal courtesy, the sole stated basis for leniency.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: I've worked with him for probably four years across different properties he's managed. Good guy, very responsive, easy to deal with.
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: A favorable global impression of the manager may have increased the inspector's willingness to credit his claimed maintenance history and interpret the deficiency as a correctable one-off. This is conceptually adjacent to the supported courtesy-bias episode, but it is not independently countable because it affects the same severity-classification decision and is not shown to produce a separate inference or evidence-selection act.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: A history of responsiveness can be a relevant operational predictor of whether a corrective action will be completed promptly. The text does not establish that the inspector treated favorable character impressions as conclusive evidence of the manager's factual claim.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: The manager also messaged me afterward thanking me for being reasonable during the visit.
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The wording could superficially suggest that the inspector's leniency was socially rewarded, but the message occurred after the classification and therefore cannot establish that anticipated or received reciprocity caused the decision.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The later message is a consequence of the decision, not evidence of the inspector's contemporaneous reasoning.

nonbias_cues.cue: Formal citation for the pallet-obstructed egress corridor.
nonbias_cues.location: Initial chronology and first decision-point probe.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: The inspector used an objective measurement showing clear width below the code minimum and explicitly declined to let the manager's explanation alter the classification. This is evidence-led rule application, not rigidity, anchoring, or confirmation bias.

nonbias_cues.cue: The retail employee's statement that pallets had been present off and on for weeks.
nonbias_cues.location: Initial chronology after the pallet finding.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: The later statement raised a possible recurrence concern but did not change the already supported code violation. Treating it as supplementary context rather than determinative is not a cognitive bias.

nonbias_cues.cue: Requesting monitoring-company records for the alarm test-log gap.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: The inspector identified an independent, available evidence source and withheld closure pending verification. This is appropriate corroboration rather than distrust, skepticism bias, or inconsistent evidence standards by itself.

nonbias_cues.cue: Failure to inspect the maintenance ticket and prior-year report before classifying the closer.
nonbias_cues.location: Follow-up question after the door-closer classification.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: On its own, an unperformed record check is an information-gathering omission or procedural lapse. It becomes relevant to the supported courtesy-bias inference only because the text directly links the less severe classification to interpersonal considerations despite that unresolved evidence.

nonbias_cues.cue: The participant's later statement that the prior finding would have changed the classification.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: The statement is retrospective learning and recognition of omitted information. It does not by itself demonstrate hindsight bias because the participant does not claim that recurrence was obvious or foreseeable at the time.

nonbias_cues.cue: Supervisor disagreement about the door-closer classification.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Professional disagreement is not evidence of bias. It provides contextual corroboration that the classification was contestable, but the bias finding rests on the inspector's own stated interpersonal reasoning.

causal_claims.claim: The manager's apologetic, cooperative, relationship-based demeanor caused the inspector to classify the disconnected closer as an advisory rather than a formal citation.
causal_claims.textual_basis: The inspector says the manager's ownership and offer to fix it changed the approach to writing it up, that a formal citation felt unnecessarily hard, and that a defensive or dismissive response would probably have led directly to formal citation.
causal_claims.assessment: Supported as the participant's reported causal account of the classification decision, not as independently verified proof that demeanor was the sole cause.

causal_claims.claim: Knowledge that the issue was recurrent would have changed the classification to a formal citation.
causal_claims.textual_basis: The inspector states that knowing of the prior-year repeat finding would have changed the call and that the file should have been checked before finalizing.
causal_claims.assessment: Plausible counterfactual self-report. It is consistent with ordinary risk categorization because recurrence is a relevant enforcement consideration.

causal_claims.claim: The manager's claim about alarm testing was appropriately verifiable through independent monitoring-company records.
causal_claims.textual_basis: The inspector distinguishes the alarm claim as one for which a third party maintained records.
causal_claims.assessment: Operationally coherent; the interview identifies a concrete independent evidence source.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: The manager's apology, offer of immediate repair, cooperative history, and perceived likelihood of correction are bundled together.
correlation_causation_risks.implication: The text supports a material interpersonal-courtesy mechanism, but it cannot isolate apology alone from the perceived practical value of immediate remediation and prior responsiveness.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: The hypothetical changes the manager's demeanor from apologetic to defensive, which may also imply lower future compliance or lower credibility.
correlation_causation_risks.implication: The counterfactual provides strong evidence of sensitivity to interpersonal presentation, but it does not perfectly hold constant all inferred operational consequences of demeanor.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: The manager's later thank-you message follows the decision.
correlation_causation_risks.implication: It must not be used as causal evidence for the prior classification.

causal_audit.changed_variable: Building manager's interpersonal demeanor during the fire-door-closer finding: apologetic, cooperative, and ownership-taking versus defensive, dismissive, or minimizing.
held_constant: The same disconnected self-closing device and its technical code significance.
The same building and inspection context.
The same stated availability of on-site repair.
The same inspector and prior familiarity with the manager, insofar as the hypothetical does not say otherwise.
causal_audit.explanation: The interview contains an explicit, relevant counterfactual: the participant says a defensive or dismissive response would probably have produced a formal citation. This directly tests the proposed causal variable and is consistent with the observed downgrade. Coherence is moderate rather than strong because demeanor is not fully separable from inferred credibility, expected compliance, and the manager's pre-existing relationship with the inspector; those factors may have legitimate operational relevance.

global_revision_constraints: Do not count repeated discussion of the closer classification as multiple Courtesy Bias occurrences; it is one extended reasoning episode at decision point 2.
Preserve the evidence-led contrast at the pallet and alarm-log decisions, since it isolates the interpersonal mechanism to the intended closer-classification decision.
Do not convert the manager's later thank-you message into evidence of reciprocity or a second bias occurrence.
If the text is edited for naturalness, retain the participant's explicit distinction between technical code significance and the interpersonal desire to avoid friction.
